Checking the edge measurements, the footer brand and nav are off by 28px — tracing it to padding conflicts between `.site-foot-inner`'s gutter and `.site-foot`'s baseline padding rule.

I'm wondering if the scrollbar width is throwing off my centering calculation, but the footer's grid layout with the max-width item and auto margins should center it the same regardless. I should just measure the actual bounding rectangle and computed padding directly instead of reasoning it out further.

Checking the lookbook gallery and work section dimensions confirms they're sized correctly against the main padding. But the eyebrow text is rendering at 18px instead of the expected 11px — tracing the specificity, a paragraph selector is beating the eyebrow class rule, so I need a more specific selector combining both to fix it, and there's a similar sizing issue at the 390 breakpoint too.

For hero paragraphs, the lead class is being applied to all of them, which makes sense for the homepage but causes the lookbook's secondary body paragraphs to render too large at 21px instead of 18px — I should restrict the lead styling to just the first paragraph in each hero block. Home page heading, nav, and footer sizes all check out correctly.

Checking motion transitions now, I notice the footer nav links are picking up a color transition timing that seems to come from a global anchor hover rule rather than something footer-specific.

I verify the footer logo sits correctly within the footer's bounding box and both aria-current attributes are present as expected.

For reduced motion, though, something's off — the pill and nav transitions still report .32s and the footer logo animation still runs, even though my media query guards should suppress them. This matches the baseline behavior with no guards, suggesting the `set media light reduced-motion` command in the script may not actually be emulating reduced motion in the browser.

I want to check this directly by evaluating whether `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` actually returns true after setting the media preference. For comparing screenshots against the baseline, I'm thinking through options since pixel-diffing tools may not be available — maybe I should just visually inspect them instead of relying on checksums, since lazy-loaded images will cause minor differences anyway.

I have several independent tasks to knock out now: fixing the eyebrow CSS specificity and applying lead styling only to the first hero paragraph, measuring the footer brand's 158px offset, verifying reduced-motion emulation actually works, doing a quick edge measurement with an empty stage, and viewing the after-screenshots across breakpoints. Since these are all independent, I'll just work through them all in sequence now.

Most after-state numbers check out, but I found three issues to fix: the eyebrow's specificity miss rendering at 18px, the footer brand offset at 158 instead of 130, and reduced-motion emulation not engaging. I'll fix the eyebrow, remeasure the other two, verify stage-off numbers, and review the after screenshots together.

cat > docs/design-stages.md <<'EOF'
# Design stages (preview toggle)

Three design passes from the September 2026 reviews (`.context/design-review-{1,2,3}.md`) are implemented as **additive stage stylesheets** so they can be compared at runtime until a direction is chosen.

| Stage | File | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| `v1` Layout | `src/styles/stages/v1-layout.css` | One container (`--container`, 118rem) for header, content and footer; `--gutter`; spacing scale; radius tokens on media containers; post-image and gallery-overflow fixes; single Instagram section on posts |
| `v2` Type | `src/styles/stages/v2-type.css` | Fluid type scale on the 10px root; one heading scale; `.label` / `.eyebrow` / `.lead` / `.pill` / `.section-title` roles; post h1; 18px body copy everywhere |
| `v3` Motion | `src/styles/stages/v3-motion.css` + `src/scripts/reveal.ts` | Quiet Swup crossfade, `[data-reveal]` scroll reveal, shared hover language, footer wordmark draw, reduced-motion guards, live `aria-current` |

## How it works

- Every stage selector is prefixed with `html[data-design~="vN"]`. Baseline CSS is untouched, so `<html data-design="">` is the original design.
- The attribute is set before first paint by an inline script in `src/layouts/Layout.astro` from `localStorage["lovely-sunday:design"]`. **Default is `"v1 v2 v3"`** (all stages on). Set it to `""` if production should stay on Baseline until a decision is made.
- Tokens live in `src/styles/vars.css` and are inert until a stage rule reads them.
- Markup is identical in every stage. Structural additions (post h1, `data-reveal`, `data-section`) are activated by CSS/JS per stage.

## The toggle

`src/components/DesignStageToggle.astro` renders a pill at the bottom of the page with **Baseline / All** presets and independent **Layout / Type / Motion** switches. It updates the attribute in place (no reload), persists the choice, and dispatches `design:change` so the reveal runtime re-binds.

It renders in `npm run dev` automatically. To include it in a deployed preview:

```bash
PUBLIC_DESIGN_TOGGLE=1 npm run build
```

Production builds without that variable contain no toggle markup.

## Picking a winner

1. Decide which stages ship.
2. For each winning file, delete the `html[data-design~="vN"] ` prefix (and `:global(html[data-design~="vN"])` in `InstagramGrid.astro`, `InstagramFeed.astro`, `about-lovely-sunday.astro`), then fold the rules into the baseline files they override.
3. Delete losing stage files, the inline stage script, and `DesignStageToggle.astro`.
4. Keep `src/scripts/reveal.ts` if `v3` wins (make `motionEnabled()` ignore the stage check).

## Re-capturing screenshots

```bash
STAGE="v1 v2 v3" bash .context/capture-full.sh "$PWD/.context/review-after"
STAGE="" bash .context/capture-full.sh "$PWD/.context/review-baseline-check"
STAGE="v1 v2 v3" OUT="$PWD/.context/review-after-details" bash .context/capture-details.sh
```

Three design passes from the September 2026 reviews (`.context/design-review-{1,2,3}.md`) are implemented as **additive stage stylesheets** so they can be compared at runtime until a direction is chosen.

| Stage | File | What it changes |

| `v2` Type | `src/styles/stages/v2-type.css` | Fluid type scale on the 10px root; one heading scale; `.label` / `.eyebrow` / `.lead` / `.pill` / `.section-title` roles; post h1; 18px body copy everywhere |
| `v3` Motion | `src/styles/stages/v3-motion.css` + `src/scripts/reveal.ts` | Quiet Swup crossfade, `[data-reveal]` scroll reveal, shared hover language, footer wordmark draw, reduced-motion guards, live `aria-current` |

## How it works

- Every stage selector is prefixed with `html[data-design~="vN"]`. Baseline CSS is untouched, so `<html data-design="">` is the original design.
- The attribute is set before first paint by an inline script in `src/layouts/Layout.astro` from `localStorage["lovely-sunday:design"]`. **Default is `"v1 v2 v3"`** (all stages on). Set it to `""` if production should stay on Baseline until a decision is made.
- Tokens live in `src/styles/vars.css` and are inert until a stage rule reads them.
- Markup is identical in every stage. Structural additions (post h1, `data-reveal`, `data-section`) are activated by CSS/JS per stage.

## The toggle

`src/components/DesignStageToggle.astro` renders a pill at the bottom of the page with **Baseline / All** presets and independent **Layout / Type / Motion** switches. It updates the attribute in place (no reload), persists the choice, and dispatches `design:change` so the reveal runtime re-binds.

```bash
PUBLIC_DESIGN_TOGGLE=1 npm run build
```

1	# Design Review 3 — Motion & interaction
2	
3	**Lens:** What moves on load, on scroll, on hover, and between pages? Is there one easing and duration language? Does everything respect `prefers-reduced-motion`?
4	**Captured:** 2026-09-27. Hover states captured with `agent-browser hover` then screenshot; page transition captured 120ms after clicking a nav link; reduced motion checked with `set media light reduced-motion`.
5	
6	## Inventory (computed at 1440)
7	
8	| Element | Transition | Animation | Hover effect |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| `#swup` wrapper | `0.25s` (all) | `slideUp 0.9s` from 4vh, every load | — |
11	| Header nav link | `opacity .3s, color .3s`; `::after transform .25s` | — | accent + underline grows (good) |
12	| CTA pill | `border-color .25s, color .25s, transform .25s` | — | accent border + lift 1px |
13	| Gallery frame / image | none | — | **none** |
14	| Footer nav link | `opacity .3s, color .3s` | — | accent |
15	| Inline links | `color .4s` → `.2s` on hover | — | underline + accent |
16	| Instagram cards | `transform 180ms` / `220ms` | — | scale 1.03 |
17	| Post-card (unused) | `opacity .6s, transform .6s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)` | — | scale 1.02 |
18	| Footer logo stroke | — | `footer-logo-write 5.8s` on load | — |
19	
20	Durations in use: 0.18, 0.2, 0.22, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.9, 5.8s. Easings: `ease`, `ease-out`, `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`, `cubic-bezier(.075,.82,.165,1)`, `cubic-bezier(.67,.01,.38,.98)`.
21	
22	Scroll reveal: `document.querySelectorAll('[data-reveal]').length` = 0, `.post-card` = 0, `.legacy-page-frame` = 12. **Nothing on the live site reveals on scroll.** The only observer (`Layout.astro:196-217`) targets `.post-card`, which no route renders, and it is bound once on `DOMContentLoaded` with no Swup rebind.
23	
24	Reduced motion: with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `#swup` still reports `animation: slideUp 0.9s`, pills and nav still transition, and the footer logo still animates. Only the unused `.post-card` rule and the footer stroke have guards.
25	
26	## Details
27	
28	![Nav hover](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/review-details/r3-nav-hover-1440.png>)
29	![Pill hover](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/review-details/r3-pill-hover-1440.png>)
30	![Frame hover (no change)](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/review-details/r3-frame-hover-1440.png>)
31	![Footer hover](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/review-details/r3-footer-hover-1440.png>)
32	![Swup mid-transition, 120ms after click](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/review-details/r3-swup-mid-transition.png>)
33	![After Swup navigation to /lookbook](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/review-details/r3-swup-after-nav-lookbook.png>)
34	
35	## Findings
36	
37	### 3.1 — Page transition is a blank-out followed by a 0.9s slide (High)
38	
39	120ms after clicking "Discover" the whole content area is empty cream (screenshot above): `html.is-animating .transition-fade { opacity: 0 }` drops everything, then the new page mounts and runs `slideUp` from 4vh (≈36px at 900 tall) over 0.9s with a very slow-out curve. A 4vh drift for almost a second on every page load, including the first, reads as lag rather than polish. The `transition: 0.25s` shorthand on the wrapper also animates every property, including layout ones.
40	
41	### 3.2 — No scroll reveal anywhere on the live site (High)
42	
43	The gallery frames, the hero, the CTA pills, the Instagram grid, and the footer all appear instantly. The one reveal system that exists targets a component (`PostCard`) that is only rendered in Storybook, and even there it would stay at `opacity: 0` after a Swup navigation because the observer is never rebound. The design intent (atelier-blush plan, step 10) called for cards fading in on scroll with a 0.6s ease-out and 0.1s stagger; that intent never reached the pages that ship.
44	
45	### 3.3 — Photos have no hover state; the one image effect that exists is inconsistent (Medium)
46	
47	Hovering a gallery frame (screenshot above) changes nothing. Instagram cards zoom 1.03 in 180ms in one component and 220ms in the other; the unused post-card zooms 1.02 in 600ms. The frames are `<figure>`s without links, so a zoom would be decorative only; but the Instagram cards and post images are links and should share one zoom spec. Radius currently sits on the `img`, so a zoom would break the rounded corners; Review 1 moves radius to the container to make this possible.
48

All three reviews are implemented, verified, and switchable in the preview. Nothing is committed; the working tree holds 22 changed or new files.

**The toggle.** A pill at the bottom of every page in `npm run dev` offers Baseline / All presets and independent Layout, Type, Motion switches. It flips the `data-design` attribute in place, persists in local storage, survives Swup navigation, and re-arms the scroll reveal when Motion comes back on. For a deployed preview, build with `PUBLIC_DESIGN_TOGGLE=1`. Production builds contain no toggle markup. Details are in `docs/design-stages.md`, including the mechanical steps to flatten a winning stage.

**How it is built.** Baseline CSS is untouched. Each review is an additive stylesheet whose selectors are prefixed with the stage attribute, so any combination can be compared honestly. Markup is identical in every stage. Tokens live in vars.css and are inert until a stage reads them.

**Measured results with all stages on, at 1440**

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Logo / hero copy / footer brand left edge | 78 / 130 / 60 | 130 / 130 / 130 |
| Post image | translated 350px off column | on the column |
| Lookbook gallery right edge | 1540, clipped | 1408, inside viewport |
| Legacy body copy / nav / footer bio | 10.2 / 10 / 9.5px | 18 / 11 / 14px |
| h1 on work, news, sold pages | none | one, above the image |
| Elements revealing on scroll | 0 | 19 on home, re-bound after each navigation |
| Active nav after Swup and on Contact | wrong | correct |
| Reduced motion | ignored | every transition, reveal, and stroke draw disabled |

Stage-off re-measurement reproduces the original numbers exactly. The build with the parity gate passes.

![Home, all stages](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/review-after/home-1440.png>)
![Post page, all stages](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/review-after/work-1440.png>)

**Two things to decide**

- The default stage is all three on. If production should stay on Baseline until you pick, change the default string in the inline script in `Layout.astro` to empty.
- Removing the PostCSS custom-properties plugin means dark mode now reaches forms and buttons for the first time. It looks right in the sanity shots, but the dark header logo on a dark background is a pre-existing issue outside this pass.

**Known limits.** The babes-day look route still renders its 404 capture, a content issue outside this scope. Agent-browser cannot emulate reduced motion, so that check was run with Playwright directly. The three review documents now end with Outcome sections and after-screenshots, and both capture scripts accept a stage so the comparison can be regenerated.

# Design system

The site's visual language is defined once, in `src/styles/vars.css`, and consumed everywhere else. The root is `html { font-size: 62.5% }`, so **1rem = 10px** throughout.

## Tokens

| Group | Tokens | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Containers | `--container` 118rem, `--container-wide` 144rem, `--container-prose` 72rem, `--gutter` | Header, footer, and page content share `--container`; galleries may use `--container-wide`; posts use `--container-prose`. Centre with `width: min(100%, var(--container))` or the `.container*` utilities in `layout.css`. |
| Spacing | `--space-1`…`--space-9` (0.4→9.6rem), `--section-gap`, `--block-gap`, `--grid-gap` | Section gap between page sections, block gap inside a section, grid gap for photo grids. No negative margins. |
| Type | `--text-xs/sm/md/lg/xl/2xl/3xl/display`, `--leading-tight/snug/body`, `--tracking-label/display` | Fluid clamps. Body is `--text-md`; `global.css` maps h1–h6 onto the scale with no per-breakpoint overrides. |
| Radii | `--radius-sm/md/lg/pill` | Radius lives on media containers (`overflow: hidden`), never on `img`, so hover zoom keeps its corners. The home hero arch is the one deliberate exception. |
| Motion | `--ease-out`, `--dur-fast/base/slow`, `--reveal-duration`, `--reveal-distance`, `--hover-scale` | Every transition references these. No literal durations or curves. |

## Type roles (`global.css`)

- `.eyebrow` — accent-coloured uppercase sans label (page kickers).
- `.label` — uppercase sans label: nav, footer nav, panel titles, card titles.
- `.section-title` — display face at `--text-2xl` for section headings.
- `.lead` — large intro paragraph.
- `.pill` — mixed-case sans text inside CTA pills.

## Motion (`animations.css`, `src/scripts/reveal.ts`)

- **Scroll reveal:** add `data-reveal` to an element and it fades/rises in when it enters the viewport, with a short cascade for items that enter together. `data-reveal-watch` observes without hiding (the footer uses it to start the wordmark draw). An inline script in `Layout.astro` adds `html.reveal-ready` only when `IntersectionObserver` exists and reduced motion is off, so nothing is hidden without JS. The runtime re-binds after every Swup navigation.
- **Page transitions:** Swup crossfade plus a 12px rise over `--dur-base`. Nothing animates on first load.
- **Hover:** linked media zooms by `--hover-scale` over `--dur-slow`; gallery frames use a gentler 1.01; nav and footer links grow an accent underline from the left; inline links draw a 1px underline; pills lift 1px.
- **Reduced motion:** all of the above collapse to static under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

## Header state

`Header.astro` gives each link a space-separated `data-section` list; `reveal.ts` sets `aria-current="page"` from `location.pathname` after every navigation (server-rendered for the first load).

## Build-gate constraints

Keep exactly one `<h1>` per page, keep `.legacy-page-gallery`, `.legacy-page-frame`, `.is-half-span` and `img[data-image-dimensions]` on legacy galleries, and never introduce class names or strings containing `sqs-` or `agentation`.
EOF

content.text:
Everything is done and verified. Nothing is left to request.

All three design passes are now integrated directly into the site, the toggle and stage layers are gone, and the homepage has been redesigned around Aileen's own photography. The build with the parity gate passes. Nothing is committed; the dev server is still running at http://127.0.0.1:4321.

**Integration and refactor.** The three stage stylesheets were folded into their natural homes rather than kept as overrides. `vars.css` holds the tokens, `global.css` the heading scale and type roles, `site-shell.css` the shared container and nav spec, `legacy-page.css` the gallery pages, `animations.css` the Swup crossfade and scroll reveal, and `content.css` one clean post section. Along the way I removed the duplicate post rules, the dead home-specific legacy block, the global image radius, two dead stylesheets, and the PostCSS plugin that was inlining variables. Net diff is 699 lines in, 714 out. The pill CTA and the underline link are now single roles in global.css, shared by the home page, the legacy pages, and the nav.

**Homepage.** The subagent rebuilt it in new files only, and I reviewed every file and screenshot.

- **Hero gallery.** A five-photo mosaic from Purple & Lace, Flower Crowns in Bora Bora, Lavender Dreams in Paris, Sunset in a Wheat Field, and Exploring a German Castle. The celebrity press image is gone.
- **Post list.** Twelve shoots, each showing the main image, three thumbnails, a label, and the title. Three columns at desktop, two on tablet, one on phones.
- **Photo selection.** The subagent checked every candidate page visually and excluded seven lookbook entries that turned out to be press photos, street-style pins, or shopping collages. Only your own shoots appear. Images use responsive CDN renditions with `srcset` instead of the 640KB originals.

![Homepage at 1440](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/final/home-1440.png>)
![Homepage at 390](</Users/manikrathee/conductor/workspaces/lovely-sunday/barcelona-v2/.context/final/home-390.png>)

**Verified on the final build.** One h1 per page. Header, hero, cards, and footer all start at x=130 on 1440. Nav 11px, body 18px. Post images on their column, lookbook gallery centered inside the viewport. Scroll reveal, hover zoom, and active nav state all working after client-side navigation, and all motion collapses under reduced motion. Dark mode now reaches forms and buttons. Every card image confirmed loaded.

**Two things worth knowing**

- The Instagram section at the bottom of the home page renders empty here because the Instagram scrape returns nothing in this environment. The wiring is unchanged from before.
- The lookbook index page still shows its captured mix of press and product images, which is the content of that page itself. The redesign only changed which photos the homepage chooses.

`docs/design-system.md` documents the tokens, type roles, motion rules, and build-gate constraints for future work.

definition.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms
